title: Bell Block
coordinate_convention: [row, column], zero-based; map rows are listed top to bottom
design_notes: Prepare a fresh Phi+ on entry: Level 1 ended with measured 00/11, not an entangled register. Bob applies X(q1), producing Psi+, then measures q1. Outcome m=0 leaves game |10>; outcome m=1 leaves |01>. Bob SENDs his actual observed bit and Alice explicitly RECEIVEs it. Alice chooses X(q0) for m=0, or KEEP/I for m=1, then measures q0=0. Final |00> and |01> both open both physical doors; no door tests Bob's local bit. Sequence, classical delivery and correction are gameplay prerequisites, not a Bell inequality or proof of experimental entanglement. The joint debugger is an omniscient/classical view; it is not Alice's local measurement. Alice could infer m by measuring early in ideal Psi+, but that would consume her qubit and break this protocol, so premature measurements are disabled.
integration_notes: Ten map entities: two players, two sensors, two X terminals, two physical doors and two exits. SEND BIT, RECEIVE BIT and KEEP/I are keyboard-accessible HUD console controls, not extra map entities. Sensors obey measurement_allowed per qubit. Door art/collision obey door_states. Require both players at exits after the quantum objective; classical/correction actions never submit a backend job.

narration.enter:
Fresh Bell pair. Bob applies X first.
Then Bob measures and sends his bit.
narration.first_gate:
Bob's X makes the outcomes opposite.
Bob measures before Alice acts.
narration.first_measure:
Measurement removes entanglement.
Bob must SEND; Alice must RECEIVE.
narration.correction:
Received 0: Alice uses X.
Received 1: Alice chooses KEEP/I.
narration.death:
Follow the classical message first.
Reset the stage to start again.
narration.glitch:
Backend data disagrees with ideal.
See the sampling diagnostics.
narration.win:
Alice measured 0 after correction.
Both exits unlock for 00 or 01.
